title: Kale JupyterLab extension — from annotated notebook to AI Pipeline

steps.caption: Data science projects — the abc123-user1 project hosts the Kale workbench for this lab
Workbenches tab — the kale-demo workbench runs a default data science notebook image that ships Kale
The workbench opens JupyterLab — the Kale extension ships inside the standard data science image

details.label: Kale
details.value: hidden until enabled from the terminal

steps.caption: New Terminal (command palette, the File → New → Terminal equivalent) — Kale is enabled from the workbench terminal
Enable the Kale extension — jupyter labextension enable jupyterlab-kubeflow-kale

details.label: Ships as
details.value: disabled by default in the notebook image

steps.caption: The extension registers — jupyterlab-kubeflow-kale v2.1.1 enabled OK
The documented verify step — jupyter labextension list shows Kale enabled among the image extensions
Browser refresh — the Kale UI registers in JupyterLab and the demo notebook opens
Run All Cells — Kale converts the notebook as it was executed, so cells run cleanly first
Kubeflow Pipelines Deployment Panel — Kale reports its KFP connection status here
